design.description: Six sequential multiple-ascending-dose cohorts with once-daily subcutaneous cotadutide.

studies.population: Adults with overweight or obesity and type 2 diabetes.
studies.overallDuration: 7 to 41 days of treatment, depending on cohort
studies.safetySummary: In the peer-reviewed Phase 2a portion, treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 88% of both groups. Gastrointestinal events were more frequent with cotadutide; no cotadutide recipient had a grade 3 or worse event, and there were no deaths.

studies.officialTitle: A Phase 2, Randomized, Double-blind, Placebo-controlled Study to Evaluate the Safety and Pharmacodynamic Effects of MEDI0382 in Obese Subjects With Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease (NAFLD)/ Non-Alcoholic Steatohepatitis (NASH)

design.description: Randomized 2:1:2:1 to cotadutide 300 mcg, matched placebo, cotadutide 600 mcg, matched placebo (pooled placebo group), for 19 weeks.

studies.population: Obese adults (BMI >=30 kg/m2) with biopsy-confirmed, non-cirrhotic NAFLD/NASH (NAS >=4, fibrosis stage F1-F3); participants with type 2 diabetes were eligible if HbA1c <=9.5% on stable background therapy.
studies.safetySummary: Any-grade TEAEs occurred in 37.5% (9/24) placebo, 76.9% (20/26) cotadutide 300 mcg, and 91.7% (22/24) cotadutide 600 mcg (as-treated/safety population; one patient randomized to 600 mcg completed at the lower dose and was analyzed with the 300 mcg group for safety, giving safety-population N of 26/24 rather than the randomized 25/25 -- the source publication's own Table 2 column header states "n=25" for 600 mcg, inconsistent with its own disposition figure and text, which both give n=24; entered here using the disposition-figure/text value). Serious TEAEs were balanced (1 each arm, none treatment-related: appendicitis 300 mcg, diverticulitis 600 mcg, syncope placebo). TEAEs leading to discontinuation: 4.2% placebo, 7.7% 300 mcg, 16.7% 600 mcg. No deaths.

studies.officialTitle: A Phase 2b, Multicentre, Randomised, Double-blind, Placebo-controlled, and Open-label Comparator Study of Cotadutide in Participants Who Have Chronic Kidney Disease With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus

design.masking: Double-blind for cotadutide and placebo; open-label active comparator
design.description: Randomized to cotadutide 100, 300, or 600 mcg once daily, matched placebo, or open-label once-weekly semaglutide 1.0 mg, on background standard-of-care renal/T2D therapy, for 26 weeks.

studies.population: Adults aged 18-79 years with type 2 diabetes, eGFR 20 to <90 mL/min/1.73m2, and micro- or macroalbuminuria (UACR >50 mg/g), on stable background ACE inhibitor or ARB therapy.
studies.safetySummary: Any AE and serious-AE rates were broadly similar across the cotadutide 100/300/600 mcg, placebo, and semaglutide 1 mg arms (as-treated/safety population per the source's Table 3: n=55/48/48/51/45 -- the 100 mcg safety n exceeds its own randomized n=52 elsewhere in the same publication; entered as printed, not reconciled). Serious AEs: 9.1% (100 mcg), 10.4% (300 mcg), 10.4% (600 mcg), 9.8% (placebo), 8.9% (semaglutide). Discontinuations for AE: 3.6%, 4.2%, 20.8%, 7.8%, 15.6% respectively. Two deaths occurred in the cotadutide 100 mcg arm (acute myocardial infarction; suspected suicide), neither deemed related to cotadutide. Gastrointestinal AEs (nausea, vomiting) were the most frequent class and were more common with cotadutide 600 mcg and semaglutide than with lower cotadutide doses or placebo.
